senses: height, summit, pinnacle, top, peak (since castles were often built on heights)

arx, arcis, f.
arx ab arcendo, quod is locus munitissimus rubis, a quo facillime possit hostis prohiberi, Müll; cf. ; ; Doed. Syn. IV. p. 428; v. arceo
,
a stronghold, castle, citadel, fortress, ἀκρόπολις; in Rome, the Capitolium.
Lit.: arce et urbe orba sum, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 114 Müll.): optumates, Corinthum quae arcem altam habetis, id. ap. ejusd. Fam. 7, 6: edicite per urbem ut omnes qui arcem astuque accolunt, cives, etc.; Att. ap. : Illa autem in arcem [hinc] abiit,; so : In arcem transcurso opus est,: Condere coeperunt urbīs arcemque locare,: arcis servator, candidus anser,: munire arcem,: cum Tarento amisso arcem tamen Livius retinuisset,: arx intra moenia in immanem altitudinem edita; : arx Sion,: arx Jerusalem,: Romana,: Capitolina,; cf. : Sabinus arcem Capitolii insedit mixto milite,; et saep. As the place on which auguries were received (cf. auguraculum): ut cum in arce augurium augures acturi essent,; so and 24.—Hence,
Trop., defence, prolection, refuge, bulwark, etc.: Castoris templum fuit te consule arx civium perditorum, receptaculum veterum Catilinae militum, castellum forensis latrocinii,: haec urbs, lux orbis terrarum atque arx omnium gentium,; cf. : Africa arx omnium provinciarum,: Stoicorum,: arx finitimorum, Campani,; : tribunicium auxilium et provocationem, duas arces libertatis tuendae,: arx ad aliquid faciendum,: eam urbem pro arce habiturus Philippus adversus Graeciae civitates,; : quasi arx aeternae dominationis,.—
As the abode of tyrants, a poet. designation of tyranny (cf. ), Heins.: cupidi arcium,; cf. : non dum attigit arcem, Juris et humani culmen, Corte; cf. , and 4, 800; .—
Prov.: arcem facere e cloacā,to make a mountain of a mole-hill,.—
Since castles were generally on a height, meton., a height, summit, pinnacle, top, peak (usu. poet. and in Aug. and postAug. prose), lit. and trop.
Lit.: summā locum sibi legit in arce,upon the extreme height,; cf. . —So,
